1. **`Ops` enum** (line 213): this needs a new `POW("pow")` constant whose `compute(lhs, rhs)` returns `Math.pow(lhs, rhs)`. `LOOKUP_MAP` is built from `Ops.values()`, so the constructor will then accept `fn: "pow"` without further changes.

The bug is in the anonymous `IntervalIterator` that `IntervalBuilder.NO_INTERVALS` returns from `intervals()`, in `lucene/queries/src/java/org/apache/lucene/queries/intervals/IntervalBuilder.java:240`.

- **Cause:** `docID()` (line 271) always returns `NO_MORE_DOCS`, even before `nextDoc()` or `advance()` has been called. The `DocIdSetIterator` contract requires `-1` at that point. A conjunction can therefore fail when its sub-iterators are not all on the same starting doc, for example when an interval query made only of stopwords is one of the clauses.
- **Fix:** keep a current-doc field that starts at `-1`. `nextDoc()` (line 276) and `advance()` (line 281) should set it to `NO_MORE_DOCS` and return it, and `docID()` should return that field.

The methods are in anonymous classes, so I've named them under the `NO_INTERVALS` field. I found this by reading the source and did not run any code.

The bug is in `OpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator.preceding`, which I confirmed by reading the code; I didn't run or edit anything.

- **Cause:** `preceding` starts the binary search at `sentenceStarts.length / 2` (line 151), with range `[0, length - 1]`. When `length == 2`, `currentSentence` is 1. If `pos >= sentenceStarts[1]`, `moveToSentenceAt` then evaluates `sentenceStarts[currentSentence + 1]` (line 103), which is index 2 and out of bounds. Changing the start to `(sentenceStarts.length - 1) / 2`, as the issue suggests, matches `following`.
- **Related helper:** `moveToSentenceAt` reads `currentSentence + 1` without a bounds check. It may also need hardening, because its recursion can reach the last index when the maximum is `length - 1`. For example, the midpoint calculation at line 105 can land on `maxSentence` while `minSentence != maxSentence`.

- **Cause:** line 151 of `OpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator.java` starts the search at `sentenceStarts.length / 2`. With two sentences that is index 1, the last one. `moveToSentenceAt(pos, 0, 1)` then reads `sentenceStarts[currentSentence + 1]` (line 103) whenever `pos >= sentenceStarts[1]`, which is out of bounds.
- **Fix:** use `(sentenceStarts.length - 1) / 2`, as `following` does on line 89.
- **Check alongside the fix:** changing the starting index may not be enough on its own. `preceding` searches up to `sentenceStarts.length - 1`, so the recursion in `moveToSentenceAt` (lines 97–115) can still reach the last index and evaluate `sentenceStarts[currentSentence + 1]`. For example, its midpoint formula on line 105 can move `currentSentence` to `maxSentence`. A bounds guard there is worth considering, so I've listed it second.
